source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which side effect is expected with aluminum hydroxide antacids?
questions.rationale: Aluminum compounds cause constipation; magnesium compounds cause diarrhea.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) as an antacid may cause:
questions.rationale: Magnesium compounds cause diarrhea; aluminum compounds cause constipation.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should antacids be timed with sucralfate?
questions.rationale: Avoid antacids within 30 minutes of sucralfate; give sucralfate on an empty stomach.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-PUD Drugs (PDF p. 119)
questions.quote: Avoid antacids within 30 minutes of sucralfate

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Omeprazole belongs to which drug class?
questions.rationale: Omeprazole and lansoprazole are PPIs; cimetidine, ranitidine, and famotidine are H2 blockers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-PUD Drugs (PDF p. 118)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Antidiarrheals are contraindicated in which condition?
questions.rationale: Antidiarrheals are contraindicated in ulcerative colitis (risk of toxic megacolon).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Long-term mineral oil use can reduce absorption of:
questions.rationale: Intestinal lubricants such as mineral oil inhibit absorption of vitamins A, D, E, and K.
questions.quote: Intestinal lubricants inhibit absorption of fat-soluble vitamins

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Laxatives are contraindicated with which symptom?
questions.rationale: Laxatives are contraindicated with GI obstruction, suspected appendicitis, and undiagnosed abdominal pain.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Digoxin is described as having which effects?
questions.rationale: Digoxin strengthens contraction (+ inotropic) and slows the heart rate (− chronotropic).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Glycosides (PDF p. 120)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on digoxin sees yellow-green halos. What does this suggest?
questions.rationale: Visual changes with yellow-green halos (xanthopsia) suggest digoxin toxicity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Glycosides (PDF p. 121)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the antidote for digoxin toxicity?
questions.rationale: Digoxin immune Fab (Digibind) is the antidote.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Glycosides (PDF p. 121)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on digoxin should report which weight change?
questions.rationale: Daily weights; report a 2-lb (about 1 kg) increase, which may indicate fluid retention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Glycosides (PDF p. 121)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Losartan belongs to which antihypertensive class?
questions.rationale: Losartan, telmisartan, and irbesartan are ARBs; captopril and enalapril are ACE inhibitors.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which teaching prevents orthostatic hypotension with antihypertensives?
questions.rationale: Clients are taught to change positions slowly and follow a low-sodium diet.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a contraindication to streptokinase?
questions.rationale: Thrombolytics are contraindicated with active bleeding, cerebral hemorrhage, recent surgery, and severe hypertension.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the antidote for thrombolytic-induced bleeding?
questions.rationale: Aminocaproic acid, a fibrinolysis inhibitor, is the antidote for thrombolytics.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on atorvastatin should report which symptom?
questions.rationale: Statins can cause muscle tenderness or weakness and liver dysfunction; LFTs are monitored.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is a nitroglycerin patch used to prevent tolerance?
questions.rationale: Remove after 12–14 hours to allow a 10–12 hour patch-free interval; apply to hairless areas and rotate sites.
questions.quote: remove the patch after 12-14 hours, allowing 10-12 "patch-free" hour

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chest pain persists after 3 sublingual nitroglycerin tablets over 15 minutes. What next?
questions.rationale: Give one tablet every 5 minutes up to three; if no relief after 15 minutes, notify the physician immediately.
questions.quote: If pain is not relieved after 15 minutes and three tablets, notify physician immediately

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How often should sublingual nitroglycerin be replaced?
questions.rationale: Replace approximately every six months and protect from heat and light.
questions.quote: Replace drug approximately every six months

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which teaching is given for beta blockers?
questions.rationale: Beta blockers are not discontinued abruptly; take the pulse first and take at the same time daily.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Beta Blockers (PDF p. 124)
questions.quote: Not to discontinue the drug abrupt

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on a calcium channel blocker becomes constipated. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: Increase fluids to counteract constipation; limit caffeine and avoid alcohol.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Calcium-Channel Blockers (PDF p. 125)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which drug is used for anaphylactic shock?
questions.rationale: Epinephrine treats anaphylactic shock; dopamine and dobutamine treat hypovolemic and cardiogenic shock.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypotension and Shock (PDF p. 125)
